```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(AKCatchments)
```

This vignette runs the package on a network of sites, from a table of
sample points to a GeoPackage of catchments with their attributes,
uncertainty columns and provenance, plus the long tables (daily weather,
snow-off, projections) that go with them. It says where the time goes,
what can run in parallel, and what to set. Nothing here is run when the
vignette is built.

## 1. Where the time goes

| step | function | what limits it | parallel? | recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DEM window per site | `ak_catchments()` | download (IfSAR service, Copernicus tiles) | yes: sites or windows | `regional = TRUE` for clustered sites; daemons |
| conditioning (breach, D8) | `ak_catchments()`, `import_catchments()` | CPU (WhiteboxTools) | yes: sites or windows | daemons; WhiteboxTools threads are shared out |
| watershed, polygon, diagnostics | `ak_catchments()` | CPU, small | with the site | |
| reference flowlines | `ak_catchments()` | download | with the site | `flowlines = NULL` for a quick first pass |
| check plot | `ak_catchments()` | imagery download | with the site | `plot = FALSE` for reruns; plot the final set once |
| statewide maps (land cover, alder, PRISM, Pastick, geology) | layer functions | one large download, then fast | no | `ak_prefetch()` once; extraction is seconds |
| terrain attributes | `ak_topography()`, `ak_outlet_slope()` | CPU, reading the site's rasters | yes: sites | daemons |
| positional draws | `ak_permafrost()`, `ak_glaciers()` | CPU (GEOS) | yes: sites | daemons |
| soils | `ak_soils()` | one web query per site | yes: sites | 4 daemons at most (one server) |
| fire perimeters | `ak_fire()` | one query for the area | no | cached; `refresh = TRUE` after a fire season |
| Daymet | `ak_weather()` | hundreds of small requests | concurrent requests | automatic, 4 at a time (`AKCatchments.max_active`) |
| MODIS snow-off | `ak_snowoff()` | 740 MB per year, once | no | `keep_full = TRUE` on a shared cache |
| SNAP projections | `ak_climate_projection()` | one request per coverage and block | yes: coverages | 4-6 daemons (one server) |
| Landsat NDVI | `ak_peak_ndvi()` | thousands of scene reads | yes: groups of nearby catchments | daemons; first run takes hours |

Two things follow. First, delineation and the web-bound layers are limited
by downloads more than by computing, so more processes help only until
the server or your connection is the limit: in the November 2026 live
tests, two processes delineated about 1.4 times as fast as one. Sharing
DEM windows between nearby sites (`regional = TRUE`) cuts the downloads
themselves, which helps whatever the number of processes. Second, the
cache makes every second run fast: point it at a drive with room (or a
shared folder) once, and prefetch the statewide files.

Every delineation records its step times (`t_dem_s`, `t_condition_s`,
`t_watershed_s`, `t_finish_s`, `t_flowlines_s`, `t_plot_s`, `t_total_s`),
so after a first run you can see which step to work on:

```{r timing, eval = FALSE}
sf::st_drop_geometry(x) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(dplyr::starts_with("t_"), sum)) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(dplyr::everything(), names_to = "step", values_to = "seconds") |>
  dplyr::mutate(share = round(seconds / max(seconds), 2))
```

## 2. Setting up parallel processing

The package uses the mirai package through `purrr::in_parallel()`. You
start the background processes ("daemons"); every per-site loop in the
package then uses them, and runs in this session when there are none. The
package never starts or stops daemons itself.

```{r daemons, eval = FALSE}
mirai::daemons(4)                    # 4 background R processes
mirai::status()                      # how many are connected
# ... run the workflow ...
mirai::daemons(0)                    # stop them
```

How many:

- **CPU-bound steps** (conditioning, terrain, positional draws): up to the
  number of physical cores less one. WhiteboxTools is multithreaded
  itself, so each process is given `cores %/% daemons` threads
  (`options(AKCatchments.wbt_threads = )` to override): the machine is used
  fully either way, and parallel sites mostly help with the steps that are
  not WhiteboxTools.
- **Web-bound steps** (DEM windows, Soil Data Access, SNAP, Landsat): 4-6.
  Each daemon is another connection to the same server; more is slower,
  or gets you throttled.
- **Memory**: each process holds one site's (or one window's) rasters,
  up to a few hundred MB for the largest catchments at 5 m. With 16 GB,
  4 daemons is a safe start; regional windows are larger, so use fewer
  daemons with `regional = TRUE` on big clusters.

The daemons load the **installed** package. After changing the source,
reinstall (`devtools::install()`); under `pkgload::load_all()` the loops
run sequentially, with a message. Results are the same either way:
random draws are seeded per site, not per session.

Progress: every loop shows a progress bar naming the site (or cluster, or
coverage) it is on. For a log of a long batch job, set
`options(AKCatchments.verbose = TRUE)` for one line per finished site
with its time.

## 3. The run

### 3.1 Cache and prefetch

```{r cache, eval = FALSE}
ak_set_cache("D:/AKCatchments_cache", persist = "user")   # once per machine
pts <- read.csv("cakn_sites.csv")      # site_code, lat, lon; optional ref_area_km2, snap_dist_m, dem_source, ...
```

The RGI glaciers come from NSIDC, which needs a free Earthdata Login in a
`.netrc` file; every other layer downloads without an account.
`vignette("data-sources")`, section 2.1, sets it up.

The statewide files are prefetched after delineation (they need the
catchments' extent), or now from a rough area:

```{r prefetch, eval = FALSE}
area <- sf::st_as_sf(pts, coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  sf::st_buffer(20000) |> sf::st_union() |> sf::st_sf(site_code = "area", geometry = _)
ak_prefetch(area)                       # land cover, alder, PRISM, geology, permafrost, glaciers, fire perimeters
```

### 3.2 Delineate

```{r delineate, eval = FALSE}
mirai::daemons(4)
x <- ak_catchments(pts, regional = TRUE, plot_dir = "plots/delineation", keep_delineations = TRUE)
x                                       # delin_ok and flags
attr(x, "errors")                       # sites that failed, and why
table(x$window_mode)                    # which sites shared a window
```

Look at every plot in `plots/delineation`. For sites with
`delin_ok = FALSE`, or that look wrong, add a `ref_area_km2`, a larger
`snap_dist_m` or another `dem_source` in the points table and rerun those
rows; or draw the catchment by hand and import it (3.4).

The first time, compare the two delineation paths on your sites:

```{r compare-paths, eval = FALSE}
x_site <- ak_catchments(pts, regional = FALSE, plot = FALSE)
compare_catchments(x_site, x) |> dplyr::arrange(iou) |> head()   # expect IoU near 1
```

### 3.3 Compare with your reference polygons

```{r validate, eval = FALSE}
hand <- sf::read_sf("hand_catchments.gpkg")
compare_catchments(x, hand) |> dplyr::arrange(iou)   # IoU, area ratio, Hausdorff, agree
```

See `vignette("delineation")`, section 4.

### 3.4 The final set of polygons

```{r final, eval = FALSE}
fixed <- import_catchments(sf::read_sf("hand_fixes.gpkg"))   # conditions their DEM too
x <- dplyr::bind_rows(x[!x$site_code %in% fixed$site_code, ], fixed)
x <- import_catchments(x, condition = FALSE)                  # one object again, with provenance
```

### 3.5 Attributes: one value per site

Each function appends its columns, with uncertainty columns and a
provenance row:

```{r layers, eval = FALSE}
x <- x |>
  ak_topography() |>
  ak_outlet_slope(points = pts) |>
  ak_landcover() |>
  ak_alder() |>
  ak_alder(source = "nps_wrst") |>
  ak_permafrost() |>
  ak_permafrost(source = "pastick2015") |>
  ak_glaciers() |>
  ak_geology() |>
  ak_soils() |>
  ak_fire() |>
  ak_climate_normals()
ak_provenance(x)
attribute_reliability(x)                 # how much of each variable's spread is error
```

### 3.6 Long tables: by day, year, model, sample

```{r tables, eval = FALSE}
samples <- read.csv("cakn_samples.csv")   # site_code, sample_date, ...
w  <- ak_weather(x, years = 1990:2024)    # concurrent pixel requests
so <- ak_snowoff(x, years = 2001:2022, weather = w)
ws <- weather_at_samples(w, samples, snowoff = so)   # anomalies vs the 1991-2020 daily normal, melt, degree days
x  <- ak_climate_normals(x, "daymet4", weather = w)  # the same normal, as monthly columns

dl <- ak_climate_projection(x, seasons = ak_seasons(months = FALSE)[c("annual", "jja", "djf")],
                            periods = list(`2041-2070` = 2041:2070))
x  <- catchment_join(x, projection_ensemble(dl, wide = TRUE))

g  <- ak_peak_ndvi(x, years = 1985:2024)
x  <- catchment_join(x, peak_ndvi_summary(g, trend_years = 1985:2024))
fw <- ak_fire(x, samples = samples)        # burned share in windows before each sample year
mirai::daemons(0)
```

### 3.7 Write it out

```{r write, eval = FALSE}
ak_write(x, "cakn_catchments.gpkg", weather = w, snowoff = so, samples = ws,
         projections = dl, ndvi = g, fire_windows = fw)
```

The GeoPackage holds the polygons with every column, the provenance of
everything in it (product, version, download dates, arguments, and which
table each row belongs to), the per-site errors, and each table. That is
the unit to archive or hand on.

### 3.8 Cite the data

```{r cite, eval = FALSE}
refs <- ak_citations(x, layers = c("weather_daily", "snowoff", "climate_projection", "greenness"),
                     bibtex = "cakn_catchments.bib")
unique(refs$acknowledgement[nzchar(refs$acknowledgement)])   # text some providers ask for
```

`ak_citations(x)` cites the layers recorded in `x`'s provenance; the long
tables carry their own, so add them with `layers` (or pass each table as
`x`). The BibTeX file goes into a reference manager; `vignette("data-sources")`
has each provider's terms.

## 4. Rerunning

Everything downloaded is in the cache, and the conditioned rasters stay
with the delineations, so a rerun (new sites, a fixed polygon, another
layer) downloads only what is new. To refresh one source after its
provider updates it, pass `refresh = TRUE` to that function (fire
perimeters after a fire season; SNAP or Landsat to start over).
